main_issue: Whether Agent D may wear her prayer-bead bracelet covered under her sleeve (the rule says 'visible'), or whether it must be fully removed for tomorrow's shift

A-B.evidence: B asks if the bracelet is included and says 'she has to take it off' (2, 4); B says it must be off, not hidden (16); A: 'Agent B's right' (17).

A-C.evidence: C says covered settles it (7); A: 'No, it has to be off' (8). Repeated clashes, ending with A: 'End of discussion' and C: 'You're not head office' (27-28).

A-D.evidence: D offers to cover or tape it (13, 15) and pleads on religious grounds (22); A refuses: 'Not hidden, not taped' (17), 'it has to come off' (23).

B-C.evidence: B says it must be off, not just hidden (16); C insists 'visible' means covering is fine (19, 21). They oppose each other's position but do not address each other directly.

B-D.evidence: B: 'she has to take it off' (4) and rejects D's taping idea (16); D says she can't take it off (13, 22).

C-D.evidence: C asks if D can cover it (5); D agrees (6); C backs her ('She said she will cover it', 21) and D promises to keep it covered (13).
